#PSYCH 221a Project - Visualizations
##Gabriel Hammond 


```{r Load data}

H1 <- read.csv("Data/Processed_Data/h1.csv")

H2 <- read.csv("Data/Processed_Data/h2.csv")

```



```{r H1 Visualization}

#H1: Male sex will predict higher rates of prior infection with disease (sum of pathogen prevalence scores) compared to female sex because testosterone suppresses immune function

ggplot(H1,
       aes(x = Sex_birth,
           y = path_sum,
           fill = Sex_birth)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_violin() +
  labs(x = "Sex at Birth",
       y = "History of Infection")


#My hypothesis does not appear to be supported. Ignoring the intersex boxplot (likely skewed by a small sample size), the male and female distributions appear to be largely similar. 

```

```{r H2 Visualization}

#H2: An increased degree of political difference in a relationship will predict lower relationship happiness because of the difficulty of reconciling opposing worldviews in domestic settings.

ggplot(H2,
       aes(x = pol_diff,
       y = prqc_3)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  geom_jitter() +
  labs(x = "Political Difference in Relationship",
       y = "Relationship Happiness")

#Here my hypothesis does appear to be supported, relationships that have a lesser degree of political difference appear to report higher relationship happiness, and vice versa. 

```
